title: Practice 5: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Ты ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)) на танцы с Соней?
exercises.why: **пойдешь** — future tense (2nd person singular) of пойти: the perfective of йти, «set out».
exercises.prompt: Will you be going to the dance with Sonya?

exercises.q: ___ (сбегать — to run there and back) в булочную за хлебом!
exercises.why: **сбегай** — imperative (ты, singular) of сбегать: the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.
exercises.prompt: Run and get some bread from the baker's!

exercises.q: Мы ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) в ресторан.
exercises.why: **сходили** — past tense (plural) of сходить: the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.

exercises.q: Я хочу ___ (поездить — to ride about for a while) по Европе.
exercises.why: **поездить** — infinitive, the perfective of ездить meaning «for a while».
exercises.prompt: I want to travel around Europe.

exercises.q: Том за словом в карман не ___ (полезть — to start climbing).
exercises.why: **полезет** — future tense (3rd person singular) of полезть: the perfective of лезть, «set out».
exercises.prompt: Tom is never at a loss for words.

exercises.q: Все ___ (поплыть — to start swimming, set sail), кроме Тома.
exercises.why: **поплыли** — past tense (plural) of поплыть: the perfective of плыть, «set out».

exercises.q: Я хочу ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) в парк.
exercises.why: **сходить** — infinitive, the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.
exercises.prompt: I want to go to the park.

exercises.q: Меня впервые ___ (повести — to lead off, take along) в цирк.
exercises.why: **повели** — past tense (plural) of повести: the perfective of вести, «set out».
exercises.prompt: I was taken to a circus for the first time.

exercises.q: Я решила туда ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)).
exercises.why: **сходить** — infinitive, the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.
exercises.prompt: I made up my mind to go there.

exercises.q: Давайте ___ (поплыть — to start swimming, set sail) к плоту.
exercises.why: **поплывём** — future tense (1st person plural) of поплыть: the perfective of плыть, «set out». Давай — one person (ты); Давайте — several people, or one person by вы; the verb is the same.
exercises.prompt: Let's swim out to the float.

exercises.q: Якитори ___ (походить — to walk about for a while) на шашлык.
exercises.why: **походит** — present tense (3rd person singular) of походить: the perfective of ходить meaning «for a while».

exercises.q: The driver skidded on a slippery road and collided with the crash barrier.
exercises.why: **повело** — past tense (neuter) of повести: the perfective of вести, «set out».
exercises.ru: Водителя ___ на скользкой дороге, и он врезался в ограждение.

exercises.q: Давай ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) на рынок!
exercises.why: **сходим** — present tense (1st person plural) of сходить: the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. Давай — one person (ты); Давайте — several people, or one person by вы; the verb is the same.

exercises.q: Я ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) к венерологу.
exercises.why: **сходил** — past tense (masculine) of сходить: the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.

exercises.q: Я ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) к венерологу.
exercises.why: **сходила** — past tense (feminine) of сходить: the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.

exercises.q: Её имя часто ___ (слетать — to fly there and back) с его губ.
exercises.why: **слетало** — past tense (neuter) of слетать: the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.
exercises.prompt: Her name was often on his lips.

exercises.q: Джон за словом в карман не ___ (полезть — to start climbing).
exercises.why: **полезет** — future tense (3rd person singular) of полезть: the perfective of лезть, «set out».

exercises.q: Его здоровье ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)) на убыль.
exercises.why: **пошло** — past tense (neuter) of пойти: the perfective of йти, «set out».
exercises.prompt: His health has begun to decline.

exercises.q: Он по-пластунски ___ (поползти — to start crawling) в сторону.
exercises.why: **пополз** — past tense (masculine) of поползти: the perfective of ползти, «set out».
exercises.prompt: He crawled to the side on his belly.

exercises.q: Итиро впервые ___ (поехать — to set off (by vehicle)) в Нагою.
exercises.why: **поедет** — future tense (3rd person singular) of поехать: the perfective of ехать, «set out».
exercises.prompt: Ichiro will go to Nagoya for the first time.
